claim: Under SSP5-8.5, nearly half (48.6%) of global mangroves face High or Very High composite risk by 2100
Under SSP2-4.5, 19.4% of mangroves face High or Very High risk
SLR is the dominant risk driver at most mangrove locations
56% of mangroves are exposed to major tropical cyclones (Cat 3+)
Under SSP5-8.5, 99.3% of mangroves experience SLR rates >=7 mm/yr (deficit highly likely threshold)
Caribbean and Pacific Island nations are most at risk
Cuba has the largest mangrove area (342,417 ha) at 100% High+Very High risk under SSP5-8.5
At-risk mangrove area increases from ~29,000 km2 (SSP2-4.5) to ~73,000 km2 (SSP5-8.5)
SE Asia & Australia and Pacific Islands have highest regional CRI under SSP5-8.5
Meeting Paris Agreement targets (SSP2-4.5) would significantly reduce mangrove risk compared to SSP5-8.5
